meaning_en: A 'proponent' is someone who advocates for something — a supporter.
'Quash' means to void/suppress/annul; 'Nullify' is the closest synonym.
'Cognoscenti' means people with expert knowledge/connoisseurs in a particular field.
'Reckless' means acting without care for consequences; 'Rash' is the direct synonym (the others mean cautious).
Chaotic, turbulent and disorderly are all synonyms of 'tumultuous' (marked by disorder and upheaval).
A truce is an agreement to stop fighting, i.e., a cessation of hostilities. Skirmish, onslaught and contention all denote conflict, the opposite.
To compensate means to make up for or offset a loss or deficiency.
'Colossal' means extremely large; 'Small' is the direct antonym.
'Intrinsic' means inherent/natural; 'Acquired' (gained externally) is its antonym.

'Engender' means to give rise to/cause something. 'Cause' is a synonym, not an antonym. Among the remaining options, 'Subdue' (to suppress/quell) is the closest antonym, representing the opposite action of bringing something into being.
'Malevolent' means wishing harm to others; 'Benevolent' (kind, well-meaning) is its direct antonym.
By elimination, 'malevolence' (ill will, malice) is the opposite of generosity's benevolent spirit. Altruism and largesse are synonyms of generosity, and 'general' is unrelated.
An analogue is something similar or comparable, so 'difference' is its antonym. Correlate and cognate imply similarity or relatedness.
Amusement is a state of enjoyment; 'melancholy' (deep sadness) is its opposite. The other options do not express the contrasting emotion.
'Abnegate' means to renounce or give up (a right, belief or pleasure); 'Renounce' is the synonym.
'Nebulous' means vague, hazy or ill-defined; 'Vague' is the synonym.
A bibliophile is a lover or collector of books.
Juvenile means immature or childish in manner, so 'Childish' is the closest synonym.
Callow means young and inexperienced; 'Inexperienced' is the closest synonym.
Apogee means the highest or culminating point; 'Peak' is the closest synonym. 'Nadir' is its opposite.
Implacable means unable to be appeased or pacified, hence 'unyielding'. Soft, flexible and gentle convey the opposite.
Propitious means giving a good chance of success, i.e. 'favorable'. Doubtful, harmful and unlucky convey the opposite.
To illuminate means to light up or, figuratively, to clarify or make clear. 'Explain' captures the figurative sense. Darken and hide are antonyms.
Garrulous means excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters; the synonym is 'talkative'. Reserved and silent are opposites.
Intransigent means unwilling to change one's views or compromise; the synonym is 'stubborn'. Willing, compliant and submissive are opposites.
'Luminous' means emitting or full of light, bright. 'Radiant' (shining brightly) is the closest synonym. Dull, Dim and Opaque are antonyms.
'Exiguous' means very small in size or amount, meagre. 'Scanty' matches it. Huge, Excessive and Abundant are opposites.
'Haphazard' means lacking order or planning, done at random. 'Random' is the synonym; Organized, Intentional and Planned are antonyms.
'Rebellious' means defiant or resisting authority. 'Disobedient' is the synonym; Submissive, Obedient and Agreeable are antonyms.
A 'Eulogy' is a speech or piece of writing in high praise of someone. 'Tribute' matches it; Criticism, Insult and Condemnation are opposites.
'Cogent' means clear, logical and convincing; the synonym is 'Convincing'.
'Invective' is abusive or insulting language; the synonym is 'Tirade'.
'Ebullient' means cheerful and full of energy; the synonym is 'Enthusiastic'.
'Complaisant' means eager to please/agreeable; the closest synonym here is 'Submissive'.
'Felicitous' means well-chosen or apt for the occasion; the synonym is 'Appropriate'.
'Dilatory' means slow to act or delaying; the synonym is 'Tardy'.
'Cadaverous' means resembling a corpse, pale and gaunt; the synonym is 'Pale'.
'Coruscate' means to flash or sparkle; the synonym is 'Sparkle'.
'Transhistorical' means existing or valid across all historical periods, i.e., not limited to any particular time â€” closest in meaning to 'timeless'.
In the given sentence, 'minute' (pronounced my-NOOT) means extremely small/tiny. This same adjectival sense is used in 'every minute detail', whereas the other options use 'minute' as a unit of time.
synonyms: The camera captured every minute detail of the insect's wing.

meaning_en: In the given sentence, 'wave' means a hand gesture of greeting. This same sense is used in 'the crowd gave a slow wave', whereas the other options use 'wave' to mean an ocean/water wave.
synonyms: The crowd gave a slow wave as the parade passed by.

meaning_en: In the given sentence, 'saw' is the past tense of the verb 'see'. This same sense is used in 'I saw a beautiful sunset', whereas the other options use 'saw' to mean the cutting tool.
synonyms: I saw a beautiful sunset last night.

meaning_en: "Teleological" relates to explanations based on purpose or design, matching "Purpose-driven."
"Epistemic" relates to knowledge or the theory of knowledge, matching "Knowledge-related."
"Surrender" means to give up or yield to another's control, matching "Yield."
"Mindfulness" means a state of active, conscious awareness, matching "Awareness."
'Historiographical' relates to the writing of history or historical study, i.e., historical writing.
'Aporetic' describes a state of puzzlement or being at a loss/full of doubt, i.e., conflicted.
'Palimpsestic' relates to a palimpsest, a manuscript with multiple layers of writing, i.e., layered.
'Provenance' means the place of origin or earliest known history of something.
'Mythopoeic' means having the capacity to create or generate myths; 'myth-making' is its direct synonym.
'Alma mater' refers to the school, college, or university that a person has previously attended.
synonyms: A school or college that one has attended

meaning_en: A 'gourmand' is a person who takes great pleasure in eating and enjoys food, often in large quantities.
synonyms: A person who loves and enjoys food

meaning_en: 'Dread' means great fear or apprehension, making 'fear' its closest synonym.
'Renounce' means to formally give up or reject a belief, claim, or activity; 'reject' is its closest synonym here.
'Wisdom' refers to deep understanding and good judgment, making 'knowledge' its closest synonym among the given options.
'Pernicious' means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way; 'malicious' is its closest synonym here.
'Existential' relates to existence and its meaning, a concept central to philosophy, making 'philosophical' the closest synonym.
'Eternal' means lasting forever or without end, closest in meaning to 'infinite'.
'Clout' means influence or power, especially in politics or business.
A 'suspect' is a person thought to be possibly guilty of a crime.
synonyms: A person who is believed to be involved in a crime

meaning_en: A 'mirage' is an illusion or something that seems real but isn't, close in meaning to 'fantasy'.
'Contumacious' means stubbornly disobedient or rebellious against authority; its opposite is 'obedient'.
'Sanguine' means optimistic or cheerful; 'melancholic' (gloomy, sad) is its opposite.
'Disparate' means fundamentally different or distinct; 'similar' is its antonym.
'Evanescent' means quickly fading or short-lived; 'enduring' (lasting) is its opposite.
'Abstruse' means difficult to understand; 'clear' (easy to understand) is its opposite.
'Somnolent' means sleepy or drowsy; 'awake' is its direct opposite.
